title: Eval-harness: suite selector helpers for Optimize gating (quantization/batching/caching) + workload tags
author: Olivia Grant
release_notes: Eval-harness now exposes stable suite-selection helpers for Optimize gating, mapping optimization types + workload tags to required eval suites and minimum sample size defaults.
body:
Title: Suite selector helpers for Optimize gating (quantization/batching/caching) + workload tags

Context
Optimize quality guardrails need a deterministic way to select the right eval suites for a proposed config change. Today, suite selection is implemented ad-hoc in downstream callers (and in a couple of internal scripts), which has already drifted: quantization transitions used a stricter suite set than batching/caching changes, and workload variants (tool calling vs structured output) were not consistently tagged.

This PR adds a small, opinionated suite selector module in eval-harness that:
- maps (optimization_type, workload_tags, model_family) -> required_suites
- returns structured metadata used by the gating runner ("why this suite")
- centralizes workload tags and provides validation / canonicalization helpers

Scope
- Add OptimizationType enum: QUANTIZATION, BATCHING, CACHING (future: ROUTING).
- Add WorkloadTag registry and canonical parsing (case-insensitive; stable string ids).
- Add suite selection helpers with stable default sets + explicit overrides for known risk areas.
- Add unit tests covering selection determinism and tag validation.

Key behaviors
- Quantization changes always include: format/structure checks + reasoning regression sentinel + any model-family specific suites (e.g. llama-family vs mixtral-family differences).
- Batching/caching changes include: ordering/streaming correctness suite + structured output compliance when tag present.
- Tool calling workloads include: tool schema adherence suite + function selection accuracy suite.
- Structured output workloads include: JSON schema conformance suite (strict parsing).
- If workload_tags is empty, selector returns the conservative "generic-chat" set and logs a warning in the selection metadata.

API (new)
- eval_harness/suites/selector.py
  - select_suites(optimization_type: OptimizationType, workload_tags: list[str], model_family: str | None, overrides: SuiteSelectionOverrides | None) -> SuiteSelection
  - normalize_workload_tags(tags: list[str]) -> list[str]
  - validate_workload_tags(tags: list[str]) -> None (raises ValueError with actionable message)

Example usage
Callers (Optimize gating runner) can do:
- selection = select_suites(optimization_type="QUANTIZATION", workload_tags=["tool-calling", "structured-output"], model_family="llama")
- selection.suites -> ["core.rubric.task_success", "sentinel.formatting", "sentinel.reasoning", "tool_calling.schema_adherence", "structured_output.json_schema", ...]
- selection.metadata -> includes (resolved_tags, selection_version, rationale_by_suite)

Selection versioning
This PR introduces a selection_version string ("2025-01-17") embedded in SuiteSelection. This is not a full config-driven versioning system; it’s a lightweight marker so downstream systems can attribute gating outcomes to a particular selection mapping.

Files changed (high level)
- eval_harness/suites/selector.py (new)
- eval_harness/suites/workload_tags.py (new)
- eval_harness/suites/catalog.py (minor additions: suite ids + aliases)
- eval_harness/suites/__init__.py (exports)
- tests/test_suite_selector.py (new)
- tests/test_workload_tags.py (new)
- docs/gating_mode.md (add section on suite selection inputs/outputs)

Why in eval-harness vs control plane?
We debated putting this mapping in the Optimize service / control plane, but keeping it in eval-harness:
- keeps suite semantics close to suite definitions
- ensures selection is identical for CI, ad-hoc runs, and production gating
- avoids re-implementing tag validation in multiple services

Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Add ROUTING optimization type once routing deltas are represented as a first-class config delta in the gating request.
- Add per-suite default minimum sample sizes (currently returned as "recommended_min_samples" at the selection level; the threshold engine still controls enforcement).
- Add richer model_family detection (callers currently pass this explicitly).

Review notes
- Please focus review on: suite sets per optimization type, workload tag naming, and determinism guarantees.

Checklist
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Backwards compatible (no changes to existing eval suite execution)
- [x] Selection deterministic across Python versions (explicit sorting + stable tag canonicalization)

Linked
- Linear: ENG-3922 (Batching/caching changes: define guardrail-specific eval suite selection)
- Linear: ENG-3921 (Quantization transitions: enforce additional requirements)

---
Conversation

Jonas Weber (review): The suite list looks good, but I want to be sure we’re not silently accepting unknown tags and producing a weak suite set. Can we fail closed for unknown tags?

Olivia Grant (author): Agree. I updated validate_workload_tags() to raise with a message listing allowed tags + closest matches. For backwards compatibility, normalize_workload_tags() still canonicalizes known aliases, but unknown values are rejected unless callers explicitly pass overrides.allow_unknown_tags=true (defaults false).

Sofia Ivanova (review): For batching/caching, we should include streaming/order sentinel even if workload tags omit streaming. Ordering regressions are common with continuous batching changes.

Olivia Grant (author): Added "sentinel.streaming_order" to the base set for BATCHING/CACHING regardless of tags. Also added a test that ensures it’s always present.

Jordan Lee (review): selection_version: please make sure it’s not used as an enforcement input anywhere; it should just be audit/attribution.

Olivia Grant (author): Confirmed in docs and code comments. It’s metadata only.

Selene Huang (approval): Looks good. Thanks for centralizing this; it’ll reduce drift and make triage easier.
